canonical_name: Redlock (antirez, 2014) as redlock-py, with Debian's redis-server as the lock store -- a lease-based distributed mutex, and the design Kleppmann's 2016 analysis argued is unsafe for correctness-critical use
lineage: A LEASE-based distributed mutex: acquire a key with a TTL on a majority of N independent Redis instances within a validity window; release by a check-and-delete script. Proposed by Antirez (redis.io/topics/distlock, 2014); criticised by Martin Kleppmann ('How to do distributed locking', 2016) for depending on bounded clock drift and process pauses, with Antirez's reply ('Is Redlock safe?'). Preserved as a runnable lease mechanism AND as a documented contested design (Phase 9: incorrect timing assumption).
version: github.com/SPSCommerce/redlock-py master as of 2026-09-13 (commit in hashes); redis-server 7.0 (Debian bookworm) at run time
compiler_or_interpreter: python 3.11 + redis 7 (docker python:3.11-slim with apt redis-server)
entry_points: Redlock([{host,port}...]).lock(resource, ttl_ms) -> Lock(validity, resource, key) | False; unlock(lock)

example.command: three redis instances on loopback; two clients contend for one resource
example.output: exactly one holder at a time; the second acquires only after release or TTL expiry (the ORACLE); the lease's validity window printed

upstream_docs: Sanfilippo, Distributed locks with Redis (Redlock), redis.io 2014
Kleppmann, How to do distributed locking, 2016-02-08

human_capability_summary.built_to: grant one client at a time exclusive access to a resource across machines, with a lease so a crashed holder cannot block forever
human_capability_summary.pressure: crashes of holders, network delay, clock drift, process pauses (GC) -- the last two are exactly the contested assumptions
human_capability_summary.success_means: mutual exclusion while the lease is valid; liveness after a holder dies

human_environmental_pressure: partial failure, unbounded delay, unsynchronised clocks
human_failure_condition: two holders at once after a pause or clock jump (Kleppmann's scenario); or permanent blocking without a lease
behavioral_entry_point: shorten the TTL below the holder's work time and observe the second client acquire while the first still believes it holds the lock

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run redlock-py-redis-2014
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: grant one client at a time exclusive access to a resource across machines, with a lease so a crashed holder cannot block forever
